segments.title: Chương 170: 0170 【Bạn bè cũ muôn nẻo đường đời】
segments.content:
Chapter 173: 0170 The Different Fates of Old Classmates (Bonus chapter for Alliance Leader Qing Deng Gu Fo Yi Zhan Lao Jiu Yi Zhi Yan)

"This kind of helmet? And there's only one?"

Chen Guiliang took the shit-yellow construction helmet, really wanting to ask Officer Tan to give his father a lesson.

The Road Traffic Safety Law was officially promulgated last year!

Chen Xinghua paid it no mind. After his son was seated, he started the motorcycle and took off, "It's all the same. This kind of helmet is very safe."

Chen Guiliang asked, "You didn't get a driver's license either, did you?"

"Motorcycles need a driver's license?" Chen Xinghua was quite surprised.

At this time in rural areas, nobody really got a license to ride a motorcycle; they didn't even know such a thing existed.

Chen Guiliang sighed, "Find some time to go get one, and buy two proper helmets as well."

"Alright." Chen Xinghua agreed at once.

This was by no means a perfunctory reply; he would definitely go get a license.

Because with a license, he would feel more legitimate. He could even pull it out to show off. None of the other motorcycle riders had one, so how cool would it be if he was the only one?

Chen Xinghua maneuvered the motorcycle along the rugged, uneven village road. "Yang Shuo has been demobilized and is waiting for a job assignment. His old man came looking for me a few days ago, asking if you could help arrange a job for him."

"I'll get in touch with him," Chen Guiliang said.

Yang Shuo's original name was Yang Wei. Because his classmates made fun of it, he changed his name in junior high.

He was a year older than Chen Guiliang, and they had been in the same class from elementary to junior high.

When Yang Shuo was bullied, Chen Guiliang had even stuck up for him and gotten into fights.

Later, when Chen Guiliang was cornered by someone with a knife, Yang Shuo got scared and ran to a nearby shop to call the police. After making the call, he hid inside, too afraid to come out.

Afterward, Chen Guiliang didn't blame him, but Yang Shuo felt very guilty, thinking he hadn't been a loyal friend.

He didn't have the courage to face Chen Guiliang and would deliberately avoid him whenever they saw each other.

Soon, it was time for the high school entrance exams, and Chen Guiliang went off to high school.

Yang Shuo, on the other hand, went to a auto repair shop as an apprentice, then enlisted in the army in the latter half of the year. They hadn't seen each other since, only exchanging two letters. One of them even included a photo of him in his military uniform.

The kid was quite unlucky. After two years of mandatory service, he became a non-commissioned officer, but only a year and a half after the promotion, he ran into the last major round of military downsizing.

In another timeline, Chen Guiliang roughly knew the trajectory of his life. His job placement after demobilization never materialized, so Yang Shuo went to work at a repair shop, and later partnered with someone to open his own.

When Chen Guiliang used to watch *Soldiers Sortie*, he would always subconsciously think of Yang Shuo, because Yang Shuo had been laid off as a tank crewman.

The motorcycle suddenly stopped.

Due to the terrain, Chen Xinghua's attempt to show off fell flat.

He had his son get off and walk while he slowly rode the motorcycle up onto the ridge between the fields.

The ridge was quite wide, and an experienced driver could ride across with a passenger. But Chen Xinghua wasn't confident in his own skills, so he only dared to ride slowly by himself, occasionally tapping the ground with his toes, afraid of tipping over.

After crossing the ridge, there was a steep hillside.

Chen Xinghua carefully rode to the mountain pass, breaking out in a sweat. He had finally overcome the challenge in his mind.

"Hahaha!"

Seeing his dad's expression, Chen Guiliang couldn't help but laugh.

There wasn't much danger. If the bike tipped over on the hillside, there was farmland planted with crops on both sides. If it tipped over on the ridge, at worst he'd fall into the paddy field and get covered in mud.

"Big Brother, Liangliang!" Second Aunt greeted them enthusiastically.

However poorly she had treated them in the past was matched by how eager she was to please them now. She even took the initiative to help Chen Guiliang's parents with their farm work.

Second Aunt did all this with just one request in mind: for Chen Guiliang to help out her son.

After passing Second Aunt's house and another neighbor's, they crossed the mountain pass and started going downhill again. Chen Guiliang's home was on the midslope, and further down were bamboo groves, forests, and the riverbank.

Nestled against the mountains and by the water, surrounded by lush greenery, the scenery was as picturesque as a painting.

Of course, it was completely different a few years ago. There weren't as many trees, and the river was too dirty to look at.

After the great flood of '98, a soil and water conservation policy was implemented for the middle and upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Land along the river was required to be returned to forest, and there were grain subsidies for planting trees, so the riverbanks turned green.

As the local factories closed down one after another, the river water also became clear.

Only then did the present idyllic scenery come into being.

As soon as Chen Guiliang returned here, he felt completely at ease, the hustle and bustle instantly washed away.

"Come over and give me a lift!" Chen Xinghua shouted.

To get the motorcycle into their own yard, it had to cross a drainage ditch on the side of the house. The slope was a bit steep, making it difficult for one person, so he needed Chen Guiliang to lend a hand.

While helping, Chen Guiliang teased, "Riding this bike of yours is quite a hassle."

Chen Xinghua said, "I'm planning to replace the stone slab over the ditch with a wider one, then I can push it across by myself."

"When are you going to rebuild this house?" Chen Guiliang asked, pointing at their dilapidated home.

Chen Xinghua said, "Let's wait another two years. Me buying a motorcycle and rebuilding the house at the same time would make people too jealous. It doesn't leak anymore during heavy rain; I fixed the roof last winter."

Grandma and Mom were inside watching TV and came out together when they heard the noise.

His mother, Yao Lan, had also followed the trend and gotten a perm with wavy curls, and she was wearing a pair of gold stud earrings. This was probably one of her dreams from when she was a migrant worker.

Mm, she and Dad made a good match, like city dwellers from the 90s.

Grandma hadn't changed at all, wearing a set of old clothes that had been washed until they were faded. They had bought new clothes for her, but she just kept them in the wardrobe and wouldn't wear them.

"Meow."

Panda-er let out a cry, spinning in circles in the yard, as if trying to get Chen Guiliang's attention.

But when Chen Guiliang walked over, it darted into a pile of firewood under the eaves.

"Grandma."

"Mom."

Chen Guiliang called out with a smile. His mom came over to take his luggage, while his grandma stood under the eaves, smiling at him.

After entering the house, Chen Guiliang didn't bother with anything and just flopped onto the bed, limbs spread out.

It was an old straw mat that had been used for many years, with some parts re-woven with bamboo strips. Underneath the mat lay last year's straw, which was soft and still smelled of hay.

Lying at home felt so good, more comfortable than a hotel mattress.

After putting the things away, his parents came over to talk to Chen Guiliang, telling him about recent events in the town and village. They also mentioned that the town's leaders had made a special trip to the village to inspect the agriculture and had specifically stopped by Chen Guiliang's house.

A village cadre even wanted to help his younger uncle apply for subsistence allowance, but his uncle gave him an earful.

His younger uncle had his pride too and resolutely refused to admit he had a problem.

They then talked about their relatives in the city. Grandma hadn't planned on celebrating her birthday, but they had all arranged to come over together, forcing Chen Xinghua to host a banquet at the last minute.

Through it all, his parents' message was clear: they were living a life of prestige now.

Chen Xinghua said, "Some people came to borrow money, but I only lent to one family. Lai Shunqiang from the second hamlet. His son has a tumor in his head and needs to go to Rongcheng for surgery. He's only 15, it's really pitiful. Luckily they found it early and there's still a chance. I lent him 5000 yuan and told him not to spread it around. He probably won't."

"That's money that should be lent," Chen Guiliang said.

As they talked, he fell asleep.

He woke up as evening approached and continued to lie in bed. He didn't go to help with cooking, thoroughly enjoying the bliss of being cared for by his family.

It felt exceptionally good.

It was summer, so after dinner, there was still plenty of daylight left.

"Dad, let me ride your bike," Chen Guiliang called out.

Chen Xinghua tossed the keys over first, then asked, "You know how to ride?"

"I do."

For a short ride in the village, there was no need to bring up licenses.

Chen Guiliang rode the motorcycle up and down the slopes, across the field ridges, leaving Chen Xinghua stunned as he watched.

Once on the village road, people would greet him from time to time.

He also saw a female classmate from elementary and junior high school, washing diapers by the roadside with a baby on her back. She had gone to work on the coast early on, got pregnant by her boyfriend, who then ran off just before she was due. She had no choice but to have the baby and bring it back to her parents' home to raise.

When the old classmates' eyes met, the feeling was rather poignant.

The female classmate forced an awkward smile, her expression extremely embarrassed. After a brief chat, she lowered her head and went back to washing the diapers.

Riding to the vicinity of Yang Shuo's house, Chen Guiliang yelled at the top of his lungs, "Wei-ge!"
